gaps: No existing tool stores Uber Eats buyer history locally or answers spend and frequency questions offline
Replay scripts print raw JSON with no typed exit codes, no pagination loop, and no cookie redaction
patterns: Replay the website's own getPastOrdersV1 RPC with the browser cookie jar and the literal x-csrf-token: x header
Paginate with lastWorkflowUUID and stop when meta.hasMore is false

novel_features.name: Local order-history mirror
novel_features.description: Walk every page of getPastOrdersV1 and mirror orders plus line items into SQLite, incrementally by default.
novel_features.rationale: The website shows ten orders per screen with no export; a local mirror is the only way to query years of history.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Run it once and every other command works offline in milliseconds.

novel_features.name: Order history queries
novel_features.description: List synced orders newest-first with date bounds, or fetch one order with its line items by id.
novel_features.rationale: Agents need stable ids and bounded lists, not a scrolling web page.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Stable UUIDs and date filters make follow-up questions cheap.

novel_features.name: Spend by month or year
novel_features.description: Sum order totals into monthly or yearly buckets from the local mirror.
novel_features.rationale: Uber Eats offers no spend report at all.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Answers 'how much did I spend on delivery this year' in one call.

novel_features.name: Most-ordered items
novel_features.description: Rank line items by quantity across every synced order, with order counts and spend.
novel_features.rationale: Reorder suggestions in the app are opaque; this is the real ranking from your data.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Grounds 'what do I usually get' in actual counts.

novel_features.name: Most-ordered restaurants
novel_features.description: Rank restaurants by order count and total spend.
novel_features.rationale: No restaurant-level history view exists on the site.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Shows where the money actually goes.

novel_features.name: Offline text search
novel_features.description: Case-insensitive search across restaurant names and item titles in the local mirror.
novel_features.rationale: The website has no order search.
novel_features.why_it_matters: 'When did I last order X' becomes a single local query.

narrative.headline: Your Uber Eats order history as a local database — spend, favourites, and search the app cannot answer.
narrative.value_prop: Uber Eats has no public buyer API and the website only shows ten orders at a time. This CLI replays the same order-history call the website makes with your own browser session, mirrors every past order and line item into SQLite, and answers the questions the app cannot: how much did I spend last month, what do I order most, and when did I last order ramen. It is strictly read-only: it never places, tips, pays, or touches Uber rides.
narrative.auth_narrative: Uber Eats consumer endpoints are cookie-session only; the public Eats Marketplace OAuth scopes are merchant-side and cannot read a buyer's history. Sign in at ubereats.com in Chrome, then run `ubereats-pp-cli auth login --chrome` (or `--cookies-file` with a Playwright storage-state export or a raw Cookie header). Cookie values are stored with mode 0600 and never printed.
